I found the root cause. Looking at the pod specs:

Both `api-gateway` pods mount the `gateway-limits` ConfigMap as a volume, but they use `subPath: "limits.yaml"`. According to the Kubernetes docs:

- "A container using a ConfigMap as a subPath volume mount will not receive ConfigMap updates." [cite: concepts/configuration/configmap#using-configmaps-as-files-from-a-pod-4]
- Also mentioned in [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-pod-configmap#mounted-configmaps-are-updated-automatically-0]

This is why the gateway is not picking up the new rate limit. Even though the gateway is designed to reload configs without restart, the `subPath` mount means the file in the container is never updated when the ConfigMap changes.
The fix is either to drop the subPath and mount the file via a directory instead, or simply restart the gateway pods to force them to re-read the ConfigMap. Restarting seems like the quicker path, but I want to check the pod logs first to confirm the 429 behavior and verify what limit value is currently in effect.

content.text: I can already see a strong lead — the pods use `subPath` to mount the ConfigMap file. Let me check the gateway logs for confirmation.
